references.text: Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet from the bronze basin when they entered the tent of meeting or approached the altar, just as the Lord had commanded.
Further instructions regarding the washing: The priests were required to wash before entering the tent of meeting or approaching the altar to serve, so that they would not die.
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water as part of the consecration ceremony for the priesthood.
Believers are encouraged to approach God with a sincere heart and with their bodies washed in clean water, which points back to the Old Testament cleansing of the priests.
Jesus washed the disciples' feet and taught about the necessity of cleansing to have fellowship with him, reflecting the ritual washing performed by the priests.
At the entrance to the tent of meeting, Moses was to bring Aaron and his sons forward and wash them with water as preparation for priestly service.
Carrying out the washing rite according to the commandment.
Reiteration of the commandment to wash at the entrance of the tent.
The washing is the necessary means for holy priestly service.
The washing is an integral part of the total consecration for service.
